correctness.rationale: Spectral Cauchy--Schwarz proves an upper bound at every vertex, and a stationary resolvent column attains it exactly. Periodized massive resolvents give a closed coth formula. Strict loss follows from coth(x)<1+1/x and tanh(y)<y. Global parameter localization is proved before uniform derivative expansions; strict local concavity then yields eventual uniqueness, and Taylor coefficients 3/2, 3/8, 1/16 are independently recomputed. Direct spatial and spectral checks pass for 11 small cycles; asymptotic checks extend to size 100000. No numerical result is substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact Green and general interpolation tools are acknowledged as earlier literature. The new mathematical assertion is the evaluated finite mean-zero cyclic sharp mixed-norm defect with three fractional-power coefficients and maximizing parameter. No equivalent statement or dominating result was found after comparing same-space homogeneous, cycle resolvent, infinite-lattice interpolation, and the nearest published-finding corpus claims. The incomplete 2009 source is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2009 article has a potentially broad title and was not available in full text; a hidden evaluated finite-cycle asymptotic cannot be ruled out.

The scalar mass-parameter variational approach derives from known general theory; the novelty claim is specifically the sharp finite-size expansion and optimizer scaling, not the Green representation alone.
Unindexed equivalent finite-volume asymptotics may exist.

value.rationale: The finite-cycle sharp interpolation constant is a natural stability invariant for zero-mean periodic difference equations. Quantifying the gap to the infinite-lattice constant reveals a noninteger 2/3 exponent, an exact coefficient, two higher corrections, and localization length N^(1/3) of maximizing Green profiles. The exact equality classification and asymptotic optimize a previously studied mass-parameter Green functional rather than merely rename an established inequality.
